title: st.pydeck_chart selection events (on_select="rerun") are never delivered when the chart is inside [USER].fragment
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`st.pydeck_chart(..., on_select="rerun", key=...)` never delivers the selection event to the server when the chart is rendered **inside a `[USER].fragment`**. Clicking a pickable object does nothing: no fragment rerun, no app rerun, no selection state, no console error. Hover picking (auto_highlight + tooltip) works normally, so WebGL picking itself is alive — only the selection event pipeline is dead.

The exact same chart **outside** a fragment works perfectly.

Reproduced on **1.56.0 and 1.59.1** (Windows 11, Python 3.14, pydeck 0.9.x, Chromium via Playwright and real Chrome).

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import pydeck as pdk
import streamlit as st

hexes = ["87a8100d9ffffff", "87a8100dbffffff", "87a8100c1ffffff"]  # neighbors, São Paulo

def chart(key):
    layer = pdk.Layer(
        "H3HexagonLayer",
        data=[{"hex_id": h} for h in hexes],
        id="hexes",
        get_hexagon="hex_id",
        get_fill_color=[0, 150, 255, 160],
        pickable=True,
        auto_highlight=True,
    )
    deck = pdk.Deck(
        layers=[layer],
        initial_view_state=pdk.ViewState(latitude=-23.55, longitude=-46.64, zoom=9),
        map_style=None,
    )
    ev = st.pydeck_chart(deck, on_select="rerun", key=key, height=400)
    objs = getattr(getattr(ev, "selection", None), "objects", {}) or {}
    st.write(key, "->", "SELECTED_OK" if objs else "NO_SELECTION")

st.subheader("Outside fragment — clicking a hexagon WORKS")
chart("outside_fragment")

[USER].fragment
def frag():
    st.subheader("Inside [USER].fragment — clicking a hexagon does NOTHING")
    chart("inside_fragment")

frag()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `streamlit run app.py`
2. Click a blue hexagon in the **first** (outside-fragment) chart → `SELECTED_OK` appears.
3. Click a blue hexagon in the **second** (inside-fragment) chart → nothing happens. No rerun (the running indicator never appears), no selection, no browser console error, no server log.

### Expected Behavior

Clicking a pickable object inside a fragment should trigger the fragment rerun and populate `event.selection.objects`, like it does outside a fragment (and like other selection-enabled elements, e.g. `st.plotly_chart`, do inside fragments).

### Current Behavior

The selection event is silently dropped. Hover highlight and tooltips keep working, which makes this quite hard to debug in a real app — the map looks alive but clicks go nowhere.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version (our production app, whose pydeck chart has lived inside a fragment since May 2026, had working clicks on older Streamlit builds; after rebuilding with a current version the clicks died with no code change).

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.56.0 and 1.59.1 (both reproduce)
- Python version: 3.14 (also 3.11)
- Operating System: Windows 11 / Debian 13 (Docker)
- Browser: Chrome / Chromium

### Additional Information

Found while debugging a production dashboard where the pydeck chart + click handler live inside `[USER].fragment` for rerun-cost reasons. Removing the decorator (chart inline in the page) immediately restores click delivery — that is our current workaround.

comments.body:
This is a **bug** report (flagged as a **regression**): `st.pydeck_chart(..., on_select="rerun", key=...)` silently drops selection (click) events when the chart is rendered inside `[USER].fragment`, while hover picking/tooltips keep working and the exact same chart works outside a fragment. In the frontend the click path is `handleClick` (`DeckGlJsonChart.tsx`) → `setSelection` → `useBasicWidgetClientState` → `widgetMgr.setStringValue(..., { fromUi: true }, fragmentId)` → `scheduleFlush(fragmentId)` → `sendUpdateWidgetsMessage(fragmentId)`. Inside a fragment the only difference along this path is that `fragmentId` is a defined string that is threaded into the *batched* macrotask flush, so the most likely culprits are the widget-update batching in `WidgetStateManager.scheduleFlush` (it keeps a single `scheduledFragmentId` per macrotask and coalesces updates, which can mishandle a mix of `undefined` (outside-fragment) and defined (inside-fragment) fragment IDs) and/or the dynamic-key element-id changes in #13703.

Notably, there is already an e2e test `test_pydeck_chart_selection_in_fragment` (`e2e_playwright/st_pydeck_chart_select_test.py`) that clicks a single in-fragment `H3HexagonLayer` chart and passes. The reporter's repro differs in that it renders **both** an outside-fragment chart and an inside-fragment chart on the same page simultaneously — a scenario the current tests do not cover — which is a strong lead for reproduction. Suggested next step: reproduce with the two-chart layout and confirm whether the fragment-scoped rerun is being dropped/mis-scoped during batched flushing.

### Related Issues

- [#9527 — Flickering Dataframe when using st.fragment, but only when `on_select` is provided](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9527): Same theme of a selection-enabled element (`on_select`) misbehaving specifically inside `[USER].fragment`.
- [#10308 — altair.selection_point value ignored in st.altair_chart if on_select="rerun"](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10308): Another case of `on_select="rerun"` selection state being silently dropped/ignored (different chart element).
- [#11971 — SelectboxColumn in data editor not working when fragment with run_every is active](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11971): Widget interaction breaking inside a fragment, similar fragment/widget-event interplay.

---
*This is an automated triage comment using `claude-opus-4-8-thinking-xhigh`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*

Thanks for the detailed report and the self-contained repro :pray:

I tried to reproduce this on a clean environment and **could not** get the selection event to drop — the in-fragment `st.pydeck_chart` selection is delivered correctly in every sequence I tried.

I've deployed your repro (both charts, outside vs. inside `[USER].fragment`) here so we can compare across environments: **https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-15941** — could you open it on the machine/browser where you see the problem and let me know whether the *second* (in-fragment) chart switches to `SELECTED_OK` when you click a hexagon?

### What I tested

- **Streamlit 1.59.1** (the released wheel, exact version you tested), pydeck 0.9.3, Python 3.13, macOS, headless Chromium.
- I ran your **verbatim repro** (São Paulo H3 hexes, `map_style=None`, default `selection_mode`, both charts sharing `id="hexes"`), plus a deterministic variant with known hexagon pixel coordinates.
- Interaction sequences driven with Playwright:
  - click a hexagon in the outside-fragment chart, then click a hexagon in the inside-fragment chart
  - click **only** the inside-fragment chart on a fresh page
  - rapid successive clicks on both charts

### Result

| Sequence | inside-fragment result |
|---|---|
| outside → inside | ✅ selection delivered |
| inside only (fresh page) | ✅ selection delivered |
| verbatim repro, inside only | ✅ selection delivered |

In all cases `event.selection.objects` was populated and the fragment reran; the outside chart correctly stayed unselected when only the inside chart was clicked.

I also checked the frontend path the event flows through (`handleClick` → `setSelection` → `widgetMgr.setStringValue(..., fragmentId)` → `WidgetStateManager.scheduleFlush`). The only place a fragment vs. non-fragment mix is handled is the macrotask batching in `scheduleFlush`, and it only coalesces updates fired within the **same** event-loop tick — which normal user clicks (separated by pydeck's ~200ms selection debounce) don't hit. That logic has also been in place since well before this regression window.

### Could you help narrow it down?

Since it reproduces reliably for you but not in a clean setup, it looks like it may be environment- or hardware-specific. A few things that would help:

- A short **screen recording** of the two-chart repro (so we can see the hover highlight working but the click doing nothing).
- Browser **console + network** output at the moment you click the in-fragment hexagon — in particular whether a `updateWidgets`/rerun BackMsg is sent over the websocket.
- Your exact **deck.gl / pydeck** versions and whether you're on a **software (SwiftShader) vs. hardware WebGL** context (`chrome://gpu`), since you mentioned Docker/Debian and Windows 11.
- Whether it still reproduces with `map_style=None` removed, and with a single layer id that differs between the two charts.

Happy to dig further once we can see the click event on your side. :bug:
Closing as I was also unable to reproduce the issue (echoing [USER] above)
